value: Natural processes can be studied from many different perspectives, utilizing many different methods. The ecological, short-time perspective and the evolutionary, long-term perspective have often been studied separately, but more and more the conjunction between those two is studied. It is recognized that evolutionary processes may play an important role on ecological time scales (contemporary evolution), and that ecological processes will affect the evolutionary future of populations (Stockwell et al., 2003). Selection and migration between populations are two examples of such processes, which are important both ecologically and evolutionary. The strength and shape of natural selection is determined by ecological factors, both physicchemical (temperature, habitat quality) and biological (competition, predation, pathogens). In the long run, only the genes and gene combinations resulting in individuals most adapted to these conditions will survive. Migration from an ecological perspective implies increased competition for the receiving population, and possibly increased or changed disease pressure when the migrants carry pathogens. From an evolutionary viewpoint, it means the influx of genes and new variation on which natural selection may act.

value: The nutrition of salmonid fish species use different types of fish food. In order to determine whether the fish food is a limiting factor in production, during the year of 2010, an experiment was performed based on the nutrition coefficient at the fish farm "Žunovnica" Hadzici. The examination of utilization coefficient of the Riboks 46/22 fish food was conducted in strictly controlled feeding conditions. Tested fishmeal, according to manufacturer's label (default declaration), had the conversion coefficient of 1,10 which means that 1,10 kg of fish food is required to produce 1,00 kg of meat. The experiment lasted 30 days. Standardization of the daily ration was done each day based on water temperature and total fish weight by Riboks charts. Based on the obtained nutrition coefficient of 1,11 it can be stated that Riboks 46/22 fish food contains optimal amounts of nutrients needed for growth and is not a limiting factor in the production at the fish farm "Žunovnica" Hadzici.
